subject: Private endpoint outbound stewardship: IP custody, firewall patterns, and delegated egress SOP
messages:
From: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@cleardatahealth.com, ops+infra@cleardatahealth.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints

Hi Avery / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving into network design for the private deployment and need to align on two things before our security review next Thursday:

1) Who at Redwood is the authoritative owner for the control-plane outbound IPs (for allowlisting) once the private endpoint is provisioned? We need a single point of contact to include in our firewall rules and change management.
2) A compact egress pattern we can present to corporate security: minimal destination set, port/port-range list, and a fallback policy when Redwood needs to route telemetry or auto-updates.

Attached is our starting matrix (egress-ip-matrix.csv) that lists the destination roles we expect to allow. Can you confirm which of these are stable IPs vs. regionally dynamic? Also please provide a pared-down firewall template we can insert into our ticketing system — we prefer a one-page inbound/outbound rule set rather than a multi-page runbook.

Paul
Cleardata Health

-----Original Message-----

From: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>
Sent: Monday, June 7, 2026 9:12 AM
To: Avery Johnson; Marissa Cole
Cc: security@cleardatahealth.com; ops+infra@cleardatahealth.com
Subject: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints


---

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:05:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints

Paul —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front:

- Control-plane outbound IP ownership: Redwood provides a small, documented set of static egress IPs per-region for control-plane operations; the current owner for the US region is the platform-runbooks team (cc'ed: marissa_cole). For operational changes and emergency deltas the single escalation contact is neha_kapoor@redwood.ai.
- Egress pattern: we'll provide a minimal destination list (control-plane telemetry, artifact fetch, auth token exchange endpoints) with port 443 only. No other outbound ports should be required for the control plane.

I've attached a one-page firewall template (firewall-template-v2.docx) and a populated snapshot of our egress matrix. The CSV labels column shows which entries are "static-ip", "cdn-range", or "service-fqdn" so you can decide how to represent them in your perimeter rules.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Cleardata requires IP-only allowlisting (CIDR ranges) or whether hostname-based allowlisting (FQDN) behind your proxy is acceptable for anything labeled "service-fqdn"? If you need absolute IP-only we will supply an expanded list and cadence for updates.

Avery
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints

Paul —

Adding a bit more operational context from the platform-runbooks side. Key points:

- We publish a per-region static egress IP block for the control-plane (updates are quarterly or by exception). These are intended for allowlisting in customer firewalls and are prefixed with a stable tag that appears in the CSV.
- For high-availability customers we support an optional secondary block for burst/bailover; we only fail over to that block in sustained capacity events and will notify your ops channel.
- For artifact downloads (model weights, container images) we recommend allowing the Redwood CDN ranges rather than per-object allowlisting — it reduces churn. If you cannot allowlist CDN ranges, we can provide signed gateway endpoints with predictable IPs.

Operational runbook highlights (summary):
- Ports: outbound 443 only for control-plane; outbound 80 only if you permit insecure artifact prefetch (not recommended).
- DNS: we recommend allowing DNS resolution to Redwood-managed name servers for service-fqdn entries; otherwise you will need to maintain a host-mapping table.
- Change cadence: quarterly baseline updates and immediate advisories for emergency security patches.

We're happy to land a short SLA for notification windows if Cleardata needs it.

Marissa
Platform Runbooks, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----

From: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, security@cleardatahealth.com, ops+infra@cleardatahealth.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 13:42:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints

Thanks both — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our side:

1) How will we be notified of the quarterly IP block changes? Email to the security alias is fine but we need a mechanical artifact (a signed CSV or a URL with an immutable timestamp) that we can ingest into our change control pipeline.
2) For emergency changes that may require new entries inside 24 hours, do you have an emergency roll-forward process and a contact method that guarantees acknowledgement?

Also, for the firewall template: can you make the outbound entries as "minimal as possible" with a short rationale column (one sentence) so our auditors can see why each entry exists?

Paul

---

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Paul Richmond <paul.r@cleardatahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 15:02:01 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound stewardship: IP ownership and minimal egress patterns for private endpoints

Paul —

Appreciate the questions. Operational commitments:

- Notification: We'll publish a signed CSV on our secure artifacts bucket (signed with our platform key) and a short metadata JSON that contains PublishTimestamp and SequenceNumber. The CSV URL will be stable (redirect where necessary) and we will post a notification to the security alias and the Cleardata ops webhook.
- Emergency changes: We maintain a 24/7 on-call roster. Emergency changes will follow our emergency change protocol: a ticket opened in your ticketing system (we can integrate with Jira) plus an email to your security alias and an SMS to the emergency contact. Acknowledgement is required within 1 hour for any change with a public IP delta.

Attached is the pared-down firewall template with rationale comments in the adjacent column. If Cleardata's auditors want a signed attestation for the notification process we can produce a simple statement that we follow the described cadence and contact paths.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough of the CSV and template tomorrow to lock in wording for your control records?

Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----

Yes, please schedule the walkthrough. Tomorrow 10:30am PT works for our infra lead. Also please include the signed CSV link and a short example of the Jira payload so we can validate ingestion.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing this for our security gate.

Paul
